survey: A single tall cowboy boot, shown in side profile with the toe pointing right. The shaft is tall and straight with a scalloped top. The inner lining shows at the opening, and the front is stitched in a decorative pattern. The shaft meets the foot at a stitched ankle seam. The foot runs to a pointed toe, which sits on a dark stacked sole. Under the back of the sole is an angled block heel, set in line with the heel counter. The boot floats against the background with no ground plane, which is normal for an icon. A gold spur is on the back. A rowel with spikes, held by a pin, sits on a short shank behind the heel. From there a single gold arm runs forward along the outer side of the boot at ankle height. It stops halfway along the foot, pressed against the leather. There is no heel band around the back, no strap over the instep and no buckle or button.

errors.where: Spur, gold arm on the side of the boot at the ankle
errors.what: The spur has nothing holding it on. A real spur has a U-shaped heel band that wraps around the back of the heel on both sides, plus a strap over the instep fastened with a buckle or button. Here a single straight gold bar leaves the rowel and stops in the middle of the side of the foot, as if glued on. It is a loose end with no attachment, so the spur would fall off.

fix: Make the spur a curved U-shaped metal heel band that wraps around the back of the boot heel just above the heel counter, with the spiked rowel on a short shank at the back. Have the band end on each side in a small button that holds a leather spur strap. Run the strap over the top of the instep and fasten it with a small buckle so the spur is clearly held onto the boot.
